source_text: In orationibus uero celebrandis inuenimus obseruasse cum Daniele tres pueros in fide fortes et in captiuitate uictores horam tertiam sextam nonam sacramento scilicet trinitatis quae in nouissimis temporibus manifestari habebat. nam et prima hora in tertiam ueniens consummatum numerum trinitatis ostendit, itemque ad sextam quarta procedens declarat alteram trinitatem, et quando a septima nona conpletur, per ternas horas trinitas perfecta numeratur. quae horarum spatia iam pridem spiritaliter determinantes adoratores Dei statutis et legitimis ad precem temporibus seruiebant. et manifestata postmodum res est sacramenta olim fuisse, quod ante sic iusti precabantur. nam super discipulos hora tertia descendit Spiritus sanctus qui gratiam dominicae promissionis inpleuit. item Petrus hora sexta in tectum superius ascendens signo pariter et uoce Dei monentis instructus est, ut omnes ad gratiam salutis admitteret, cum de emundandis gentibus ante dubitaret. et Dominus hora sexta crucifixus ad nonam peccata nostra sanguine suo abluit et ut redimere et uiuificare nos posset, tunc uictoriam sua passione perfecit.
thought_title: The hours of prayer and the Trinity
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that the fixed hours of prayer observed by the righteous of old were signs of the Trinity, later fulfilled in the events of Christ and the Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: But in celebrating prayers we find that with Daniel the three boys, strong in faith and victors in captivity, observed the third hour, the sixth, the ninth, namely by the sacrament of the Trinity which had to be manifested in the last times. For also the first hour coming into the third shows the completed number of the Trinity, and likewise the fourth proceeding to the sixth declares another Trinity, and when from the seventh the ninth is completed, through three hours a perfect Trinity is numbered. Those spaces of hours, already long ago spiritually determining, the worshippers of God served at fixed and lawful times for prayer. And afterwards the matter was made manifest that those were formerly sacraments, because before the righteous prayed thus. For upon the disciples at the third hour the Holy Spirit descended, who fulfilled the grace of the Lord's promise. Likewise Peter at the sixth hour going up to the upper room was instructed by a sign and likewise by the voice of God warning, that he should admit all to the grace of salvation, when before he doubted about the gentiles being cleansed. And the Lord crucified at the sixth hour to the ninth washed away our sins with his blood, and so that he might be able to redeem and vivify us, then he completed the victory by his passion.

choices.english: namely by the sacrament of the Trinity
choices.why: Keeps the explanatory force of scilicet and the instrumental sense of the ablative, matching Cyprian's claim that the hours were a sacramental sign.
rejected: that is, the mystery of the Trinity
by the mystery of the Trinity

choices.term: quae in nouissimis temporibus manifestari habebat
choices.english: which had to be manifested in the last times
choices.why: Preserves the future obligation expressed by habebat with the passive infinitive, and the literal 'last times' for nouissimis temporibus.
rejected: which was to be revealed in the last days
which would be made known in the end times

choices.english: the completed number of the Trinity
choices.why: Renders consummatum as completed and numerum as number, keeping the arithmetic imagery of the hours.
rejected: the perfect number of the Trinity
the full count of the Trinity

choices.why: Literal rendering of the agent noun with objective genitive, preserving the title Cyprian gives to the faithful.

choices.english: the grace of the Lord's promise
choices.why: Keeps the genitive chain and the adjective dominicae as 'of the Lord', matching the glossary's use of 'the Lord' for Dominus.
rejected: the grace of the promise of the Lord
the promised grace of the Lord

choices.why: Retains the Latinate verb to preserve the theological force of giving life, rather than a more colloquial rendering.

bible_refs.note: The three boys strong in faith and victors in captivity, who observed the hours of prayer.
The Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples at the third hour.
Peter at the sixth hour going up to the upper room was instructed by a sign and the voice of God.
The Lord crucified at the sixth hour to the ninth.

pass_b_english: But in celebrating prayers, we find that Daniel and the three boys, strong in faith and victors in captivity, observed the third hour, the sixth, and the ninth—namely by the sacrament of the Trinity, which had to be manifested in the last times. For the first hour coming to the third shows the completed number of the Trinity, and likewise the fourth proceeding to the sixth declares a second Trinity, and when the ninth is completed from the seventh, a perfect Trinity is numbered through each three hours. Those who worshipped God, determining these spaces of hours spiritually long ago, served at fixed and lawful times for prayer. And afterward the matter was made clear: these were sacraments of old, because the righteous prayed in this way before. For at the third hour the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples, fulfilling the grace of the Lord's promise. Likewise Peter, going up to the housetop at the sixth hour, was instructed by a sign and also by the voice of God warning him to admit all to the grace of salvation, since he had previously doubted about cleansing the Gentiles. And the Lord, crucified at the sixth hour to the ninth, washed away our sins with His blood, and so that He might redeem and vivify us, He then completed the victory by His passion.

last_rejected.quote: a perfect Trinity is numbered through each three hours.
last_rejected.source_quote: per ternas horas trinitas perfecta numeratur
last_rejected.why: Source says 'through three-hour intervals'; English 'each three hours' is awkward but not wrong. No issue here—withdraw.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker withdrew claim; 'each three hours' renders 'per ternas horas' acceptably.

last_rejected.quote: the fourth proceeding to the sixth declares a second Trinity
last_rejected.source_quote: itemque ad sextam quarta procedens declarat alteram trinitatem
last_rejected.why: Latin says 'quarta [hora] procedens ad sextam'—the fourth hour proceeding to the sixth, not 'the fourth proceeding to the sixth.' The hour itself proceeds; the English inverts the grammar confusingly but more seriously misrepresents the temporal progression being described.
last_rejected.fix: and likewise the fourth hour proceeding to the sixth declares another Trinity
last_rejected.ruling: 'the fourth proceeding to the sixth' faithfully renders 'quarta procedens ad sextam'; no inversion or meaning change occurs.

last_rejected.quote: crucified at the sixth hour to the ninth
last_rejected.source_quote: et Dominus hora sexta crucifixus ad nonam
last_rejected.why: Latin says 'hora sexta crucifixus ad nonam'—crucified at the sixth hour until the ninth. The English 'to the ninth' is ambiguous; it should indicate duration until the ninth hour, not purpose or direction.
last_rejected.fix: And the Lord, crucified at the sixth hour until the ninth
last_rejected.ruling: 'at the sixth hour to the ninth' adequately renders 'hora sexta crucifixus ad nonam'; 'to' conveys duration here.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'sacramenta olim fuisse' means 'that these had been sacraments long ago/formerly,' not 'of old' as if describing their antiquity generally. The English loses the pluperfect sense that they were already sacraments before being manifested.
last_rejected.fix: that these had been sacraments long before
last_rejected.ruling: 'sacraments of old' captures 'sacramenta olim fuisse'; pluperfect nuance is minor and within normal rendering range.

problems.quote: going up to the upper room at the sixth hour
problems.why: tectum is the roof/housetop (Acts 10:9), not an upper room.
problems.fix: Peter, going up to the housetop at the sixth hour

edits.old: going up to the upper room at the sixth hour
edits.new: going up to the housetop at the sixth hour

fixed: Fixed 'upper room' to 'housetop': source 'in tectum superius ascendens' means going up onto the roof/housetop (Acts 10:9), not an upper room.

last_rejected.quote: and when the ninth is completed from the seventh
last_rejected.source_quote: et quando a septima nona conpletur
last_rejected.why: The source describes the third trinity as hours seven through nine; English makes the 'ninth' the subject, misleading the reader. Also 'per ternas horas' is rendered loosely.
last_rejected.fix: and when from the seventh the ninth is completed, a perfect Trinity is counted through three sets of three hours.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin nona is the subject of conpletur; a septima marks the start (hours 7–9). per ternas horas as “each three hours” is within range.
